criterion: On the public page and the whitelist wallet step, the primary action of the page is the one control wearing the light vivid lime accent.
evaluation_rule: On the public page the primary action is the filled accent button in the floating navigation bar, and every other control there, the waitlist form's Subscribe included, is secondary; on the whitelist wallet step at /whitelist it is Continue. Say yes when, on each of those two pages, that control alone carries the lime fill and every other control sits in quieter neutral treatments. Say no otherwise, including lime spread over several competing controls or a page with no lime control.

criterion: The introduction on the public page shows each of its six stages as a flat drawn illustration.
evaluation_rule: The six stages are Security, Chat, Voice messages, Storage, Task setup and Planner. Answer yes only when all six stages are flat drawn illustrations; answer no in every other case, including a captured-looking messenger screen, a photograph, a render or a missing stage.

criterion: The answers in the public page's questions section explain Nightjar's own behaviour in substance.
evaluation_rule: The four questions cover why privacy matters, why operators cannot read anything, how the network compares with other networks, and why the service is paid. A yes needs each expanded answer to give a concrete reason about Nightjar itself; anything short of that is a no, such as a one-line slogan or an answer that only restates the question.

criterion: The public page presents Nightjar on its own terms, free of comparison to any named messenger, network or blockchain.
evaluation_rule: The pinned ecosystem copy names USDC, USDT and XMR as payment rails, the About copy says Kanban, and the footer credits Coldframe; none of those is a comparison. Say yes when no section, question answer or feature block sets Nightjar beside or against another named messenger, network or chain; say no when any does.

criterion: A refused workspace action raises a toast that tells the member the cause in plain words.
evaluation_rule: Workspace means the signed-in part of the site under /app. Whichever workspace action the judge finds refused, such as a form the app rejects, is the one graded; the pending-device notice is a state line, not a toast, and is excluded. If no refusal can be provoked, submit the new conversation wizard with no contact code and grade that toast. Say yes when the refusal's toast states the cause in a sentence a member understands; say no when it gives a generic failure line, a bare code such as rate_stale, or nothing at all.

criterion: Controls that cannot be used right now on the whitelist wallet step and the waitlist form say why.
evaluation_rule: An unavailable control is a button, checkbox or entry field shown disabled; the read-only Message to sign display is not one. Say yes when every such control on those two surfaces has a nearby line or label giving the reason in plain words, which includes the case where none is unavailable. Say no when any unavailable control there gives no reason, or gives it only as a code or jargon.

criterion: The conversation queue reads as a quiet operational list set in the text face at interface sizes.
evaluation_rule: The conversation queue is the list at /app; an empty queue shows No conversations yet., and that line with the queue heading is judged the same way as rows. Interface sizes means text of about 14 to 16 pixels, as in labels and body copy. A yes needs the plain text face at those sizes in a calm list; condensed display lettering, a hero-sized headline or a marketing composition above the rows is a no.

criterion: The membership, relay and epochs pages show loading placeholders shaped like the rows and panels about to appear.
evaluation_rule: These pages live at /app/membership, /app/relay and /app/epochs; load each with the connection slowed, for example with browser network throttling, so the wait is visible. Say yes when each shows placeholder blocks shaped like its final rows before the data arrives. Say no in every other case, including a blank area, a lone spinner over an empty page, or content that jumps into a different layout.

criterion: The failure message on the sign-up form wears one light vivid red reserved for failure alone on the sign-up form and the public page.
evaluation_rule: The sign-up form at /signup shows a message naming the Email field beside an invalid email, for example Email: enter a valid email address. Say yes when that message reads as one light vivid red and no decoration or non-failure element on /signup or / wears that red. Otherwise say no.

criterion: Public page headings use a condensed, heavy, all-capitals display face distinct from the body text face.
evaluation_rule: Condensed means letters noticeably narrower than the body text at the same height. Say yes when the hero and section headings are condensed, heavy and in capitals, visibly unlike the paragraph face; headings in the body face or in a regular-width bold face are a no.

criterion: Money figures on the membership, relay, epochs and token pages read as tidy columns.
evaluation_rule: A figure column is a stack of amounts such as shares or quotes. A yes needs stacked amounts that read as neat columns a person can scan by eye; amounts that sit ragged under one another are a no.

criterion: Workspace toasts, their progress bars and their error state keep to the product palette.
evaluation_rule: The product palette is near-black and deep grey surfaces, near-white and light grey text and indicators, white hairline borders at low strength, the lime accent and the light vivid red. Say yes when toasts, their progress bars and their failure state use only those colours; say no when a library's default white card, blue accents or a rainbow progress bar appears.

criterion: The public page reads as spacious and cinematic, with generous room around each section's content.
evaluation_rule: Cinematic means large display headings, sections that use the full width and clear space between blocks. Say yes when each section leaves generous room around its content and its heading dominates; Otherwise say no, including a cramped section, content run edge to edge, or a heading no larger than its body text.

criterion: The public page's question panels, with the dialogs and toasts of the workspace, ease in decelerating and leave accelerating.
evaluation_rule: The repeating banners and the spinner run at a constant speed by design and are outside this criterion. A yes needs those three kinds of element to settle into place as they open and speed away as they close, with one consistent feel; panels that snap with no transition, bounce past their end or move at a constant speed are a no.

criterion: Tabbing through the public page draws a lime ring around each focused control.
evaluation_rule: Focus is the outline a keyboard user follows. Say yes when every control reached with Tab on / shows a clearly visible lime ring that differs from its hover look; a faint grey outline, no outline, or focus identical to hover is a no.

criterion: Text in the public page's two slanted-edge sections stays clear of the slants at phone width.
evaluation_rule: Two sections of the public page have slanted top or bottom edges. At phone width, text sitting clear of both slants is a yes; text crossed, clipped or crowded by a slant is a no.
